articles.headline: Intel to Sell $15 Billion in Stock After AI Boosts Demand
articles.body: Intel announces a $15 billion stock sale to fund growth amid surging demand for AI-related chips.

articles.headline: Trump Orders Childhood Shots to Be Split Up, Citing Autism Cases
articles.body: President Trump signed an executive order recommending the combined MMR vaccine be split into three separate shots, citing autism concerns.

articles.headline: SEC Exempts Data-Center Bonds From Key Securitization Rules
articles.body: The SEC granted data-center bonds an exemption from key securitization rules, boosting financing for AI infrastructure.

articles.headline: Fed's Hammack Says Some Number of Rate Hikes May Be Needed
articles.body: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack suggested additional rate hikes could be needed depending on inflation trajectory.

articles.headline: Sergey Brin Crosses $100 Million in Spending to Fight Wealth Tax
articles.body: Google co-founder Sergey Brin has now spent over $100 million to oppose proposed wealth tax legislation.

articles.headline: Gautam Adani Wins Dismissal of US Securities Fraud Charges
articles.body: Indian billionaire Gautam Adani won dismissal of US securities fraud charges in a significant legal victory.

articles.headline: Iran Insists Strait Will Stay Closed Until U.S. Agrees to Demands
articles.body: Iran's Foreign Ministry says talks with Oman on shipping routes are separate from discussions to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz, insisting on US concessions.

articles.headline: Chip Crunch Driven by A.I. Leads to New Rush of Lobbying in Washington
articles.body: The AI-driven memory chip shortage has triggered a new wave of lobbying in Washington as tech companies seek government support.

articles.headline: Ukrainian Drone Attack Kills 13 Deep Inside Russia
articles.body: A Ukrainian drone strike on an industrial center in Tatarstan killed 13, marking one of the deadliest attacks on Russian territory since the war began.

articles.headline: Meta Unveils 'Open Source' Version of Its Most Powerful A.I. Model
articles.body: Meta released an open-source version of its most powerful AI model, intensifying competition in the AI race.

articles.headline: Private Equity Is Stuck With 33,575 Unsold Businesses
articles.body: Private equity firms are sitting on a record 33,575 unsold portfolio companies as exit markets remain challenging.

articles.headline: A.I. Agents Are Taking Entire Online Courses for Cheating Students
articles.body: AI agents are completing entire online courses on behalf of students, raising questions about the value of online degrees.

articles.headline: Oil Prices Climb on Stalemate in Strait of Hormuz
articles.body: Oil prices continued to climb as the stalemate over reopening the Strait of Hormuz persists, with Brent crude futures up 17.3%.

articles.headline: The Places Where the Bombs Have Rarely Stopped Falling in Iran
articles.body: Southern Iran continues to face relentless bombing as the US-Iran conflict drags on, devastating civilian areas.

articles.headline: As U.S. Burns Through Weapons in Iran, Russia and China Are Taking Note
articles.body: The Pentagon's rapid weapons expenditure in the Iran conflict is being closely watched by Russia and China as a measure of US military capacity.

articles.headline: Water Systems Are Ripe for Cyberattacks, Experts Warn After Suspected Iranian Hacks
articles.body: Security experts warn US water systems are vulnerable to cyberattacks after suspected Iranian intrusions in 12 states. An EPA rule that Republicans fought would address much of the risk.

articles.headline: Trump's Iran Policy Is War With Itself
articles.body: Max Boot argues that Trump's Iran policy is contradictory — simultaneously bombing Iran while demanding it reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.headline: Primary Upsets Scramble Fight for Control of Congress
articles.body: Recent primary election upsets are reshaping the battle for control of Congress ahead of the 2026 midterms.

articles.headline: AI's Memory Chip Crunch Is Now Everyone's Problem
articles.body: The AI-driven memory chip shortage is becoming a broad economic concern as supply constraints affect multiple industries.

articles.headline: China Exports Its Economic Problems to the World
articles.body: China's export surge is disguising deep structural economic weakness, with overcapacity threatening global markets.

articles.headline: 6G Is Coming. Will the West Let China Write the Rule Book?
articles.body: As 6G technology standards are developed, the West risks ceding rules-making to China's coordinated national strategy.

articles.headline: Obama Launches New Podcast
articles.body: Former President Barack Obama has launched a new podcast, adding his voice to the growing political media landscape.

articles.headline: Democrats Have a 2028 Problem
articles.body: Analysis suggests the Democratic Party faces significant structural challenges for the 2028 presidential election cycle.

articles.headline: The Big Battle for Memory
articles.body: Washington Post Intelligence examines the geopolitics of memory chip supply chains amid the AI boom.

articles.headline: Wall Street Giants Partner With Nvidia on $500bn AI Financing Deal
articles.body: Major Wall Street firms including Apollo, Blackstone, and BlackRock are partnering with Nvidia on a $500 billion AI infrastructure financing package.

articles.headline: Iranian Rhetoric Hardens Amid Push to Seal Hormuz Deal
articles.body: Iran's rhetoric is hardening as Oman-mediated talks continue over reopening the Strait of Hormuz, with Tehran demanding US compensation.

articles.headline: Greg Abel Finally Puts Buffett's Cash Pile to Work
articles.body: Berkshire Hathaway's new CEO Greg Abel ended a three-year-plus selling streak, deploying a net $20 billion into stocks.

articles.headline: Landmark Crypto Bill Stalls in US Senate Despite $225mn Spending Push
articles.body: A landmark cryptocurrency regulation bill has stalled in the US Senate despite $225 million in lobbying spending by the crypto industry.

articles.headline: Trump Revives Threat to Sack Fed Governor Lisa Cook
articles.body: President Trump has renewed threats to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, escalating tensions with the central bank.

articles.headline: Meta Told to Pay Nearly $1bn Penalty Over Social Media Harm to Children
articles.body: Meta has been ordered to pay nearly $1 billion in penalties related to social media harm to children.

articles.headline: Trump Is Dismantling US Guardrails, Warn Former Security Officials
articles.body: Former CIA and security officials are publicly warning that Trump is dismantling democratic guardrails in the United States.

articles.headline: AI Will Boost Oil and Gas Production More Than Green Energy, Report Finds
articles.body: A new report finds that AI will boost oil and gas production more than green energy, stoking debate over AI's climate impact.

articles.headline: Jeff Bezos Investor Group Closing In on Liverpool FC Stake
articles.body: A consortium led by Jeff Bezos and the son-in-law of steel billionaire Lakshmi Mittal is nearing a deal to buy a stake in Liverpool FC, valuing the club at over $6 billion.
